clue.text: Island with capital in Indonesia, a country formerly

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter of a word, so only the opening letter of the next word is wanted

blocks.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean
the first letter of Indonesia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geography note about an island whose capital lies in Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a country formerly' is the definition, not part of the wordplay: the 'a' there still belongs to the definition, while the earlier 'a' is used in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of the African state now called Zimbabwe, so it is a nation that existed historically.

blocks.note: first meaning: the heavy grey element Pb
second meaning: the strap used to walk a dog, here a setter breed

explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'setter' usually means the compiler; here it is the gun-dog breed, which is walked on a strap.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a soft heavy element and the cord or strap attached to a dog's collar for walking.

blocks.note: first meaning: in British slang to rabbit is to talk at length about nothing much
second meaning: a crisp batter cake cooked in a grid-patterned iron

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like the animal, but in British slang it is a verb meaning to chatter on (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork', talk).
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to talk vaguely and at length; as a noun it is a gridded batter cake eaten in the morning.

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

blocks.note: a sort is a kind or variety; in non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same

explanation.surface: A news item about some reported variety that people went looking for.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the past participle of seek, meaning looked for or hunted for something.

blocks.note: tho is an informal short spelling of though, meaning however
a rough figure is an approximate one

explanation.surface: A pair of contradictory words, as if something is complete yet only approximate.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough job is a total, exhaustive one with nothing left undone, as in a thorough mess.

clue.text: Link part of feature that smells

blocks.note: first meaning: a structure or connection joining two things
second meaning: the bony upper ridge of the nose, the facial feature we smell with

explanation.walkthrough: 'feature that smells' sounds like something stinking, but it is just the nose, the facial feature used for smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a span that connects two places, and also the hard top ridge of a person's nose.

clue.text: Area where the race is sabotaged

indicators.note: something sabotaged is wrecked and thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A place where somebody has deliberately ruined a race, like a vandalised horse meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of land measure equal to ten thousand square metres, so it is an area.

blocks.note: co- is the prefix for a fellow or partner, as in co-worker
a vet treats animals

explanation.surface: A wistful wish for a vet as a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet something is to want it greedily, especially what belongs to another person.

clue.text: Old adversary fairly lacking in it

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the word that follows is taken out of the synonym

blocks.note: an anti is someone opposed, an opponent
quite means fairly, as in quite good
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A complaint about an old opponent who is fairly short of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is a collectable object of considerable age, and as an adjective it means very old or old-fashioned.

clue.text: Oxygen inside part of flowering plant for a second?

indicators.note: inside places one item within the other, so the element goes into the plant part

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
the anther is the pollen-bearing part of a stamen

explanation.surface: A botany question about whether a plant gets oxygen into its flowering parts a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'a second' defines by example: a second one is one more.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for a second helping is asking for one more of the same, an additional one.

clue.text: True Democrat, European went to the polls

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for Democrat
E is the abbreviation for European
going to the polls means casting a ballot

explanation.surface: A loyal party supporter and a European both cast their ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: True in the sense of faithful and loyal, as a devoted friend is a loving and committed one.

clue.text: Featured fruit on back of bureau, like a cherry

indicators.note: the back of a word is its tail end, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: a fig is a soft sweet fruit
the final letter of bureau
cherries are typically red

explanation.surface: A still life with fruit set on top of a writing desk, one piece cherry-coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' reads as the fruit sitting on the desk; in the wordplay it simply puts the pieces in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: To feature or figure in something is to appear in it, so figured means appeared or took part.

clue.text: Triangular instrument placed with old fossil

blocks.note: to set something down is to place it
an old fossil is a dated, conventional person, which is a square

explanation.surface: An instrument laid down beside a fossil, like tools at an archaeological dig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old fossil' suggests palaeontology but is slang for a stuffy old-fashioned person.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the flat right-angled triangle draughtsmen and pupils use for drawing angles and perpendicular lines.

blocks.note: first meaning: the atmosphere we breathe, mainly nitrogen and oxygen
second meaning: to broadcast or express publicly, as with a programme or an opinion

explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like extinguish or annoyed, but here it means to broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the breathable atmosphere; the verb means to broadcast a show or voice a view publicly.

clue.text: Fuse ultimately short after setback, peaceful agreement reached

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of that word counts
a setback sets things back, so the word for short is read from right to left
after tells us the single letter is placed behind the other piece

blocks.note: curt means short or brusque
the final letter of fuse

explanation.surface: A tense stand-off where a short fuse is defused and peace is finally reached.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a ceasefire or agreement between opponents to stop fighting for a time.

clue.text: Where bowler for example hits the ground immediately?

annotation.answer: AT THE DROP OF A HAT

definitions.text: Where bowler for example hits the ground immediately?

blocks.clueFragment: Where bowler for example hits the ground immediately?
blocks.note: surface reading: a cricket bowler stumbling and falling straight to the ground
setter's reading: a bowler is a hat, and the phrase for its moment of falling means without hesitation

explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket; it is the round felt hat, and an idiom about a hat falling means instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes doing something without any delay or hesitation, as soon as a signal is given.

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A young person stirring a cup of green tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, and a teenager is someone aged thirteen to nineteen.

indicators.note: ends are the tails of words, so the closing letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the final letters of up, seductive and salsa

explanation.surface: A dance-floor scene: the pulse quickens as the seductive salsa reaches its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' suggests a heartbeat; here it is an edible seed from the legume family.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of legumes, such as lentils, beans and this small round green one.

clue.text: Load beginning to exclaim in horror

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: a fright is a sudden feeling of horror
the opening letter of exclaim

explanation.surface: Someone starting to cry out in horror under a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried by lorry, ship or train, a cargo or load.

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat, so tom means male
a hawk is someone who favours aggressive policies
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: An aggressive man hiding an advanced weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used as a tool and weapon by Native Americans.

definitions.note: collective noun for reporters as a group

blocks.note: first meaning: to pester or urge someone insistently
second meaning: journalists collectively

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'hound' invites a dog reading; the first is a verb, the second means reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to urge or harass persistently; as a noun it is journalists and newspapers collectively.

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so the second piece goes inside the first

blocks.note: to prise something open is to force it with leverage
taken as written

explanation.surface: A forceful crowd greeting someone with a cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to applaud and commend them, and the verb for that is to praise.

clue.text: Aerosol perhaps in dirty abode, inadequate

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: an aerosol is one kind of can
a sty is a filthy pigpen, or any squalid dwelling

explanation.surface: An aerosol spray in a filthy flat, not good enough to clean it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means meagre or insufficient in quantity, so barely adequate or not enough.

blocks.note: snared means caught or grabbed
rum is a spirit to drink

explanation.surface: A musician from the orchestra seizing a drink in the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orchestra member' suggests a player, but it is an instrument in the percussion section.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument is a component of an orchestra, and this is the small rattling drum in the percussion section.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, turning it round

blocks.note: as means while, as in as I was leaving
to turn is to rotate

explanation.surface: An instruction to spin something heavy while it is held up.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas giant planet is huge and spins on its axis very fast, so it is an enormous rotating body.

indicators.note: swimming suggests movement around, so these letters are jumbled
round means going around, so the jumbled letters enclose the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A char, itself a fish, swimming round an old fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Char is a real fish, which makes it look like part of the definition; it is only the letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a common European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Determined soldier, for example, behind a barrier

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so this piece is placed at the end

blocks.note: taken as written
a dam is a barrier across a river
a soldier is a type of ant, so an ant is an example

explanation.surface: A resolute soldier standing behind a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' looks military, but soldier ants are a caste in an ant colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adamant is unshakeable and refuses to change their mind, so firmly resolved.

clue.text: Does it get pig clean? Nonsense!

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: a hog is a pig, so a wash for one would clean it
second meaning: rubbish or foolish talk

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the word as two parts; originally it meant swill fed to pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an informal term for rubbish or drivel, talk that has no sense or value.

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie within the next words, spanning them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A location in Idaho named Meridian, which is a real city there.
explanation.definitionFit: Place in the sense of one's house or residence, as in come back to my place.

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed and fallen apart, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The highest tree in the wood had decayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective for the tree; it is a noun for a garment worn on the upper body.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is any upper-body garment, and a sweater, or jumper, is a knitted one.

blocks.note: a matt finish is dull rather than shiny
to hew is to shape by chopping or carving

explanation.surface: A dreary review of a book that is in poor shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first gospel of the New Testament, so a book of the Bible.
